title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Week 3 vs. San Francisco 49ers
headline: Cardinals put CB Will Johnson on IR with a neck injury that may end his season, while the run game is still a 'work in progress' ahead of a tough Week 3 game against San Francisco.
summary: LaFleur said the team has moved on from the Seattle loss and is focused on a 49ers team he called 'damn good,' with Kyle Shanahan's standard and Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw as the main defensive challenges. Will Johnson was placed on IR, possibly season-ending, because of a neck issue. The medical staff advised against playing this year, and the team is 'bracing for the worst.' Another player referred to as 'Tip' is progressing but day to day. On offense, LaFleur called the run game a 'work in progress,' with some parts working and others needing better clarity. He pointed to the balance between calling the 'perfect play' and just getting off the ball. He praised Paris Johnson for holding the offensive line to a high standard and said the unit has played some good ball but not enough against Seattle. He said Marvin Harrison Jr. is improving as a run blocker and called him his usual self, while acknowledging the outside narrative around him. He described the new 49ers defense under Raheem Morris as having Atlanta-style elements but only two games of film.

injuries.detail: Placed on IR for a neck issue that may be season-ending. The team is not prepared to have him back unless something changes.
Progressing but day to day. The name was garbled in the captions and could not be matched to the roster.

signals.claim: Will Johnson will miss the rest of the 2026 season with a neck injury.
signals.note: He is out for the year, so ARI's secondary depth takes another hit and opposing passing games may be slightly more attractive.
signals.quote: we're bracing for the worst right there

signals.note: Coaches are praising his blocking and attitude, but this says nothing about target volume.
signals.quote: I think he's been getting better and better.

signals.note: LaFleur acknowledged an outside narrative about Harrison but said he is business as usual in the building, so keep an eye on any developing situation.

topics.detail: LaFleur called it a 'work in progress' with some areas good and others needing a lot of improvement. He wants better play calls and clearer communication, and the 'cam package' mixes perfect plays with just getting off the ball.
He praised Paris Johnson for holding the group to a high standard and said the line played some good moments against a very good Seattle defense, but not enough to win.

Under Raheem Morris it has a new flavor with similarities to his Atlanta defenses and not the old 'rinse and repeat' Niners. He has only two games of film, and some of it was affected by garbage time. He praised the Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw pairing as arguably the best tandem in football.
LaFleur has great respect for Shanahan and the organization's standard, built since 2017. He said the Seattle loss was left behind after Monday's team meeting.

title: Kevin Stefanski on Atlanta Falcons preparation for Green Bay Packers matchup | Press Conference
headline: Michael Penix Jr. is back from injury and set to make his first start for ATL on Thursday night at Green Bay. AJ Terrell is lost, and Tua Tagovailoa's backup role is still open.
summary: Stefanski said the team is on a compressed Thursday-night schedule and travels to Green Bay later today. He described Penix's return as a day-to-day process built on daily check-ins and medical input. Penix did a hard workout Saturday and felt normal Sunday, which convinced him his body was ready. Stefanski agreed that no fixed Week 3 timeline existed. He said the decision on who plays was made with the latest information on who is available. The offensive game plan will center on plays Penix is comfortable with, and play caller Tommy Rees and Penix already have a good rapport. Stefanski called losing AJ Terrell tough and said the team has players who will step up, but he did not say how the secondary will be arranged. Tua Tagovailoa practiced fully and is trending in the right direction, but his status as backup is not settled. The injury report will come after today's walkthrough, since short weeks have no real practices to rule players out. He praised the Packers, their quarterback's arm talent and defensive coordinator John Gannon. He also explained that the defense wants pressure with four or fewer rushers and needs a cohesive rush plan.

title: Joe Brady Reflects On 2-0 Start, Looks Ahead To Facing The Los Angeles Chargers, And More
headline: No injury updates on DJ Moore or Ed Oliver, but Brady says he feels good about 'guys' playing Week 3; Kincaid, Palmer, Carter, Rousseau and Walker all drew praise.
summary: Brady gave no firm injury news on DJ Moore or Ed Oliver. He said several players would be limited or out of practice but he still expects them to play against the Chargers. He said the team is 2-0 but sees 'smoke detectors' on offense, defense and special teams, and wants growth from Week 2 to Week 3. On offense he pointed to too many 'get back on track' situations and said the shorter second-half passing against Houston was about establishing the run, not DJ Moore's absence. He said average depth of target doesn't matter to him and noted that two of the team's most explosive plays came on deep throws to Josh Palmer. He praised Deone Walker's offseason and scheme fit, DeWayne Carter's expanded role after Ed Oliver went down, Greg Rousseau's move to standing up on the edge, and Dalton Kincaid's expanded role. On Josh Allen, he said there is 'more there' and wants him to play within the system without taking the ball out of his hands. He previewed a tough Chargers matchup: Herbert as a complete QB, Mike McDaniel's motion-heavy offense with injuries clouding the scouting, and a strong run defense led by Khalil Mack's edge rush.

topics.detail: Brady said there is no singular issue but 'smoke detectors' across all three phases, and the team must improve from Week 2 to Week 3. The defense has had chances to get off the field, especially on third down, and the offense is living in too many 'get back on track' situations.

Brady denied that DJ Moore's exit led to shorter throws. He cited a two-minute drive with 12 personnel and a second-half focus on establishing the run, and said average depth of target is 'never important' to him.

Brady called Justin Herbert a complete quarterback who can make any throw and extend plays. He said Mike McDaniel's motions and shifts stress defensive communication, and noted the injuries make the Chargers' lineup uncertain.

Brady said the opponent's record doesn't change preparation, and the 2-0 start 'means not a damn thing right now'. He said he is pleased with the team's competitive mindset.

title: Dave Canales: 'This is a part of this process'
headline: Jonathon Brooks will have groin surgery and go on IR (6-8 week window, likely longer), making Chuba Hubbard the clear lead back with AJ Dillon the primary No. 2 and Trevor Etienne getting promoted this week.
summary: Canales said Jonathon Brooks suffered a significant groin injury, got multiple medical opinions, and will have surgery. The return timeline is similar with or without surgery, with a general window of about 6-8 weeks. The IR move frees up a roster spot. Chuba Hubbard will still handle the bulk of the carries, and Canales called the situation a great opportunity for AJ Dillon, who will be used as the second back in different roles. The team will go with one practice-squad call-up, and Trey (most likely Trevor Etienne) will be active this week and contribute in some form, including on special teams and as a returner. Devin Lloyd has a calf issue that flared up after the game, Jalen Coker's ankle is still being managed carefully, and Jaelan Phillips missed practice with a back issue. Most of the injured players are day to day and potentially playable. Canales said the run game still needs work, but he is satisfied that Bryce Young and the offense are moving the ball and scoring. He expects Cleveland to try to establish the run, and he praised the Browns' fast, young defensive front.

title: Ben Johnson talks confidence in QB room, preparing for Eagles | Press Conference
headline: Bears QB for Monday night at Philly is unsettled: Tyson Bagent is in the concussion protocol, Caleb Williams is only walking through, and Case Keenum is the one practicing.
summary: Ben Johnson said he doesn't know who will start Monday night against the Eagles. The only quarterback practicing is Case Keenum, and he said he isn't worried about calling the game for him. Tyson Bagent was placed in the concussion protocol after Sunday's game, probably from the first third-down hit, and he is out of the building. Johnson said Caleb Williams is injured, is only doing walk-throughs, and is struggling with being held back. He said he will not add a quarterback. He praised Keenum's experience and mind, and said the biggest adjustment is getting used to a different voice and cadence in the huddle. He blamed Colston Loveland's lack of targets on Carolina's coverage and protection demands, not the scheme, and said everyone on the game plan will be looked at to get involved. On the injury front, Shemar Turner and Noah Sewell started practicing, Ozzy Trapilo is no longer limited and is expected to practice in full, and Tyrique Stevenson is week to week. He also said Braxton Jones has played well and is being platooned with Theo Benedet late in games.

title: Zac Taylor Provides Injury Updates, Talks Steelers | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Andrei Iosivas is headed to IR after thumb surgery, so Cincinnati's WR and TE rooms will redistribute targets. Joe Burrow is sore, and B.J. Hill and Jonathan Allen are being managed ahead of the road game at Pittsburgh.
summary: Taylor opened with injuries. Andrei Iosivas tore a thumb ligament in the game and had surgery that morning. He goes on IR, and Taylor said it isn't season-ending but will run a bit past the minimum IR window, with no firm timeline. B.J. Hill will be worked through the week and evaluated for the game, and Jonathan Allen sat out Wednesday for load management. A sore "Joe" (apparently Burrow) was going to be monitored through practice, and Taylor wasn't specific about the cause. Taylor said the receiver and tight end rooms will have to absorb Iosivas's role, that more players will get opportunity, and that he expects them to step up, but he named nobody. Most of the session was about Pittsburgh. He praised the defensive front, T.J. Watt and Heyward's tipped balls, Patrick Graham's scheme, and the Steelers' receivers and tight ends. He also covered Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy's offense, and said the Bengals are 2-0 with no satisfaction yet. They need to clean up penalties, especially on offense, before their first road divisional game.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 23rd, 2026
headline: Browns' run game is struggling and Monken offered no personnel fixes, just 'scheme it, coach it, execute it better.' Blake Whiteheart's go-ahead TD drew big praise, and Deshaun Watson is still shaking off rust ahead of Carolina.
summary: Monken said the Browns are excited for their home opener against the Panthers after a 1-1 start on the road. He repeatedly blamed the struggling run game on scheme, play-calling and execution, said the team had to pivot to quick throws against edge pressure in the second half, and called the short-yardage sneak package 'not ready for prime time.' He said the run game is unsustainable as is, but only partly tied it to the new scheme and the five new offensive linemen. On Deshaun Watson, he walked back calling him a 'young' quarterback, saying he meant the lack of games and practice reps after injury, and that Watson needs time to rebuild confidence. He explained the low average depth of target as part of the design and partly a result of pressure, citing the early deep shot to Harold Fannin as an example. He gushed over Blake Whiteheart's touchdown catch-and-run, called him one of the hardest workers on the team, and compared him to Brock Bowers in work ethic. He praised Carolina's coaching, Bryce Young's playmaking and the Panthers' play-action and explosive plays, and noted the short week ahead of Thursday's game at Pittsburgh. No injury updates were given.

signals.claim: Whiteheart, known as a blocking tight end, is earning a bigger role as a receiver after his go-ahead touchdown.
signals.note: A TE who scored and drew heavy praise could see more passing-game looks, but he is still a blocker-first player and a touchdown-dependent fantasy option.
signals.quote: he's been diligent in getting better as route running.

signals.claim: Watson is still rebuilding confidence and rhythm after injury and will keep improving week to week.
signals.note: Monken framed Watson as still rusty, which tempers expectations for his fantasy output even though his legs help the perimeter and third-down game.

signals.claim: Fannin was the target of the early explosive downfield throw, showing the offense still wants to push the ball his way.
signals.note: It was mentioned only as an example of a deep shot, so it is a mild positive on his usage but not a clear role change.

topics.detail: Monken said the run game needs to be better in scheme, play-calling and execution, and that it is unsustainable as it stands. The new scheme and five new offensive linemen are only part of the cause. The short-yardage sneak package was poor and will be coached better.

Low average depth of throw is partly by design and partly due to pressure forcing quick throws, especially in the second half. Monken acknowledged the offense must be explosive to score and is working on third-down conversions.

Monken described Carolina as a well-coached defense with good players despite poor early stats, and praised Young's ability to extend plays and the Panthers' play action. He called containing Young and covering well down the field the challenges.

The Browns play Thursday at Pittsburgh after Carolina, and Monken will start preparing for Pittsburgh on Sunday night since he calls the plays. The priority is doing what they do best and keeping players' legs fresh.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “We Have to Be Better at What We Can Control” | Press Conference
headline: Cowboys' rookie trio of Caleb Downs, Jaishawn Barham and Malachi Lawrence is driving the defense, while the run game is struggling and Overshown has only a low chance to play vs. Baltimore in Brazil.
summary: Schottenheimer opened with injuries: Cobie Durant (hamstring) is only starting on-field rehab, P.J. Locke is out of the walking boot but still progressing, Malik Hooker is doing well, and a player referred to as 'Demo' (likely DeMarvion Overshown) has only a low probability of playing this week. Tyler Smith is working hard in conditioning and is expected back as soon as he can, though no timeline was given. He was candid that the run game is poor right now: blocking is subpar, he isn't calling many runs, and the backs are pressing for big plays. He said he's open to getting CeeDee Lamb or KaVontae Turpin more touches but called that 'not the first choice.' On defense, he praised Downs as elite, called Barham's green-dot role a sign of his intelligence while noting conditioning and rotation concerns, and raved about Lawrence's pass rush. Tyler Guyton was praised for consistent pass protection and improved run blocking at left tackle. He defended Quinnen Williams' fit in the scheme, saying he is still adjusting to the system. The game plan against Baltimore centers on containing Lamar Jackson in the pocket and not giving Derrick Henry any seams. Dak Prescott's usage won't change despite the league-wide quarterback injuries. After Brazil the team faces a short week before Houston.

title: HC Sean Payton on facing Rams in Week 3: ‘It’ll be a good challenge’
headline: Payton says RB room is fine despite one limited and one non-participant Wednesday, and he refused to discuss Jonah Coleman's reported ankle sprain; Waddle and Sutton praised as unselfish; Rams' Donald-led pass rush makes third-down protection the week's focus.

headline: No fantasy-relevant skill-player news; Campbell stressed offensive consistency (third/fourth downs, red zone) and a physical Week 3 game vs. Aaron Glenn's Jets, with Alim McNeill getting a routine rest day.
summary: Campbell opened with heavy praise for the Jets and Aaron Glenn, calling them a more talented, physical, run-committed team that wants to possess the ball and take occasional deep shots, and noting they could easily be 2-0. Asked about McNeill's heavy snap count, he blamed overtime and a short week, said ideally he and Hutchinson would play less, and said young backups (Skyler Gill-Howard, Derrick Moore and another edge player) will earn more reps as they grow. He spoke at length about Glenn's coaching and the familiarity between the staffs, expecting new wrinkles in fronts, pressures and coverage disguises, and said Detroit needs some catch-all plays. He called containing Geno Smith in the pocket a point of emphasis and rejected any trap-game idea, predicting a 60-minute brawl. On offense, he said 31 points in two games hides inconsistency: third/fourth-down conversions, a failed first-and-goal at the one against New Orleans, and self-inflicted mistakes, plus ball security against a Jets defense that forces fumbles. He also said the team added a young safety to the 53 whom they liked pre-draft for his versatility and range.

title: Kyle Shanahan Talks Brock Purdy's Player of the Week Award, Previews Cardinals
headline: Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) both sat out the first practice of Week 3, and the 49ers signed Brandin Cooks to add receiver depth, though Shanahan gave no timeline for his playing.
summary: Shanahan opened with the injury report: Mike Evans (hip), Demarcus Robinson (ankle), a player named James Thompson (ankle), and a player transcribed as "Romello white" (hand) did not practice, while Bosa, Greenlaw, Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams had vet days. CJ West has a knee bone chip and is having surgery. It is not a season-ender, and Shanahan said he has an outside chance to be available this week. The team signed veteran WR Brandin Cooks. He starts learning the offense today, and Shanahan said he has no timeline for a game debut and that Cooks must show he is one of the five receivers dressed on game day. The defensive tackle room is thin, with only two of five left, so the team signed Naquan Jones and has three practice-squad options. Shanahan praised Brock Purdy's consistency and accuracy and said the offensive line has been unbelievable, with Connor Colby playing well. He said the Cardinals under Mike are a competitive team with a Rams-style offense. He also said it is complicated to decide who goes on IR-return, with seven players on IR. Finally, he said Deebo Samuel is the same guy as before.

Shanahan said Arizona under Mike is playing hard, with a scheme similar to the Rams. He said they have more talent than people think and their defense has largely the same group as the past four years.
No sacks allowed in two games. Shanahan credited the group playing as a unit and help from the tight ends, running backs, receivers and QB.

title: Todd Bowles on Staying Disciplined: Focused on Minnesota | Press Conference
headline: Bucky Irving's running is the offense's bright spot and could anchor the game plan vs. Minnesota. An unnamed edge rusher with a groin injury missed practice, and Jalen McMillan's snaps depend on how practice goes.
summary: Bowles opened with injuries. A player asked about at the start of the session (the name was not captured) has a groin injury from the game and did not practice. Josiah Trotter's shoulder is sore, but Bowles said it has bothered him all year. Jacob Parrish was a full participant after being limited last week. If the injured edge rusher can't go, Bowles named Anthony Nelson, Al-Quadin Muhammad and David Walker as the rotation, and said it was too early in the week to know who plays. He praised Walker's sack but said Walker still has fundamentals to learn. He ruled out personnel changes among the starters, though some scheme tweaks will show up Thursday and Friday. He blamed the offense's struggles on the coaches first, said the line is still getting comfortable and that the run game is going well, and said the team will lean on whatever works, with Bucky Irving the clear positive. On the passing game, he said Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin need quick touches earlier, and that he is hopeful Jalen McMillan, who played only seven snaps as he was built up, gets more work. On defense he stressed disciplined pass rushing against Kyler Murray, tackling, batting balls, and creating turnovers. He voiced confidence in Alex Anzalone's tackling and in Ted Hurst III after a missed catch.

topics.detail: Bowles said there are no personnel changes among the starters. Some scheme adjustments will show up more Thursday and Friday.
Bowles pushed back on the idea that the defense struggles against tight ends and said it is too early to judge. He blamed the busted coverages on mental errors.

He called Brian Flores' defense chaotic, with heavy disguise and many different pressure looks. He praised Kevin O'Connell's offense as smart and complementary, and called T.J. Hockenson a dual-threat tight end who forces tough personnel choices.

Murray is expected to start for the Vikings. Bowles praised his arm, pocket accuracy and mobility, and said the pass rush must stay disciplined. He noted Murray has few snaps in this offense, which makes him an unknown.

Bowles said quarterbacks getting the ball out in about 2.5 seconds limits the pass rush, so the defense must tackle and bat balls down. The team emphasizes strip drills to create turnovers, and he said missed assignments are on both players and coaches.
The line is still getting comfortable with some new things but is running the ball well. Bowles was noncommittal on adding more intermediate passing and said the team will game plan as needed.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears (caption says "Taj") sat out Wednesday's practice with ankle soreness, and Jeffery Simmons is playing a huge snap load. Wan'Dale Robinson's targets will depend on game flow.
summary: Saleh opened by saying Tony Pollard and "Taj" (probably Tyjae Spears) would be out of Wednesday's practice with ankle soreness, while James Williams would be full. He praised Giants QB Jameis Winston's arm talent and expects New York to run its whole offense with him, and he said the Giants will come out "guns blazing" after a short week and injuries. He was complimentary of Jeffery Simmons, who had 19 pass rush wins through two weeks and played about 87% of the snaps. Saleh said ideally they would reduce that load for the long run, but Simmons is "a freaking animal." Cam Ward earned praise for protecting the ball and growing more comfortable under center and on three-step drops. Saleh expects Ward to "get a lot better." On Wan'Dale Robinson's light Sunday, Saleh said targets come from opportunity and game flow, and that the DB-heavy play-action system could make it "anyone's day." He said Cedric Gray was "there for sure" and praised the Gray, Cody Barton and Anthony Hill linebacker group. He also said the offense will face Fangio-style defenses that limit explosives, and that Tennessee's own defense plays the same way, so it is like "whack a mole." Kickoffs were another topic: he wants better coverage and expects the kicker to bounce back.

topics.detail: Saleh says Winston's arm talent doesn't change the defensive approach, and he warned Winston can put up big yardage in a hurry. He expects the Giants to run their full offense with him.
Saleh wants better kickoff coverage and wants to force returns. He backed the kicker's "dirty ball" strategy to pin teams inside the 25 and expects him to rebound from a weaker Sunday.
Saleh respects Giants DC Denard Wilson, and said familiarity with players matters little because the schemes are new. He expects a desperate Giants team coming off a short week and injuries.
Tennessee used a lot of three-step drops and under-center looks. Saleh said Fangio-style defenses give up few explosives, and Tennessee will take what's given until it can be more aggressive.
Saleh said the Week 2 game was lost in the last five minutes through lapses in detail and one-on-one battles. He called it a learning step for the young players.
